content.text:
I fixed the bug in `anthrouter/pace.py`. September 2026 in UTC now divides by 22 workdays instead of 23. I checked it only by calling `workday_elapsed_pct` directly for 15 September 2026 in UTC, which returned a 22-workday count and 45.45%. I didn't run the test suite because pytest isn't installed in this environment.

**Cause:** `period_workday_dates` took the local date of `period_end` and counted it as a workday. `period_end` is the first instant of the next month, so for UTC it counted 1 October (a Thursday).

**Fix:** the end date is now the local date of the last instant before `period_end`. I also updated the docstring to say so.

This change also affects other timezones. West of UTC (such as Los Angeles) the old end date was already the last day of the month, so those results shouldn't change. For zones east of UTC, the old code counted the first day of the next month whenever it fell on a weekday, so their counts will now drop to match the real month.
